_validation_note: 14-day window sufficient; no broadening required. Candidate 1 passed all seven gates. Key verification finding: the DOH program pages confirm 'Final funding decisions will be made by the DOH Commissioner' and 'the DOH Commissioner retains final decision-making authority on all funding decisions,' with ACF and the Advisory Council explicitly non-decisional. The CMS cooperative agreement provides federal oversight of allowable use categories but does not pre-approve individual subrecipient selections — the chokepoint is structurally clean. The scout named 'Heidi Hedberg' as Commissioner but verified DOH primary sources reference only the institutional role (Commissioner of Alaska Department of Health); the mechanism-not-actor gate is therefore strong. The $272M/year figure is the FY2026 disbursement from a ~$1.36B total cooperative agreement (RHTCMS332062, Dec 2025–Oct 2030), confirmed via TAGGS/HHS. Candidate 2 dropped on Gates 3 (OIRA layer has no named controlling actor confirmed from a primary source), 4 (no concrete Alaska AI consequence — ANC entities are explicitly exempted from the proposed change), and 5 (notice-and-comment rulemaking is a diffuse multi-actor process, not a unilateral binary). Candidates 3 and 4 dropped on Gate 1 — ADN May 18 is 26 days before June 13, outside the 21-day window (May 23 cutoff), and no in-window independent editorial story about those mechanisms was confirmed after multiple Alaska Public Media URL attempts returned 404. Candidate 5 dropped on Gate 5 — FCC Commission vote is a 5-member body and no single-actor binary decision point was confirmed.

selected_mechanism.name: Alaska RHTP DOH Commissioner Subrecipient Selection Pipeline
selected_mechanism.definition: A five-year CMS cooperative agreement ($272M/year to Alaska) in which CMS disburses funds to the Alaska Department of Health, the DOH Commissioner holds final and sole decision-making authority to approve or deny all subrecipient funding applications — including tribal health organizations and AI/technology vendors — while the Alaska Community Foundation administers intake and subawards under DOH direction and the RHTP Advisory Council is explicitly non-decisional, creating a single institutional chokepoint controlling which entities receive capital to deploy rural health AI across Alaska.
selected_mechanism.news_trigger: After sifting through nearly 1,800 funding proposals, state officials have narrowed down the potential projects to a list of just over 400. Applicants who advanced through the initial screening process have until June 22 to submit additional information. State legislator Genevieve Mina said: 'You name a program transformation, but the way that the feds designed it is almost directing us to AI.'

layers.function: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services authorizes and disburses $272,174,856/year to the Alaska Department of Health under cooperative agreement RHTCMS332062 (Dec 2025 – Oct 2030, ~$1.36B total). CMS defines allowable use categories and provides federal oversight but does not pre-approve individual subrecipient selections.
layers.controlling_actor: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

layers.function: The Commissioner of the Alaska Department of Health holds all final funding decision authority over every RHTP subrecipient application. The program page states explicitly: 'Final funding decisions will be made by the DOH Commissioner' and 'the DOH Commissioner retains final decision-making authority on all funding decisions.' The Advisory Council and ACF are explicitly non-decisional at this layer.
layers.controlling_actor: Commissioner of the Alaska Department of Health (institutional role; current incumbent: Heidi Hedberg per scout sourcing)

layers.layer_name: Alaska Community Foundation Administrative Subaward Layer
layers.function: DOH has contracted ACF to manage the application portal (Bonfire), assist applicants, issue and manage subawards for DOH-approved projects, process payments, and support compliance reporting. Administrative costs capped at 10% of total RHTP award. ACF explicitly cannot make final funding decisions — it executes DOH Commissioner approvals only.
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska Community Foundation (ACF), operating under DOH contract

layers.function: Multi-sector advisory body comprising a Steering Committee and Stakeholder Committee. Provides input on RHTP strategy and community perspectives. Explicitly non-decisional: 'The Advisory Council offers informed input but does not make funding or policy decisions.' Its non-decisional status is what consolidates all authority at the Commissioner layer.
layers.controlling_actor: RHTP Advisory Council (non-decisional — zero funding decision authority)

layers.function: Over 400 organizations advancing from the initial 1,800-proposal intake must submit detailed applications by June 22, 2026. Eligible uses explicitly include 'pilots or demonstrations of emerging technologies (e.g., AI-enabled tools or wearables).' Confirmed eligible applicant types include tribal health organizations, hospitals, and technology vendors deploying AI-powered documentation, clinical decision support, and telehealth tools.
layers.controlling_actor: 400+ applicant organizations including tribal health orgs (ANTHC, Tanana Chiefs Conference, Maniilaq Association) and technology vendors; no single controlling actor — applicants are the input pool to the chokepoint layer

chokepoint.actor: Commissioner of the Alaska Department of Health (institutional role)
chokepoint.binary_decision: Approve or deny each subrecipient application for RHTP funding — including AI-enabled technology deployment proposals. No other actor (ACF, Advisory Council, Legislature) can override or substitute for this decision within the program year. CMS oversight applies to allowable use categories, not individual subrecipient selections.
chokepoint.deadline: Mid-July 2026 (applications due June 22, 2026; selection decisions expected within approximately three weeks)

selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Alaska tribal health organizations (ANTHC, Tanana Chiefs Conference, Maniilaq Association) and AI technology vendors competing for Year 1 RHTP subrecipient awards face a single-point approval decision by the DOH Commissioner by mid-July 2026 that will determine whether Alaska's largest-ever rural health AI deployment capital infusion (~$272M/year) flows to tribal-led AI implementations or to other applicant types — setting the deployment architecture for rural health AI statewide for up to five years.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The RHTP mechanism produces a state-controlled capital allocation funnel where one institutional role — the DOH Commissioner — serves as the sole approval gateway between $272M/year in federal health transformation funds and the 400+ organizations seeking to deploy AI tools in Alaska's rural health system; because the Advisory Council and ACF are structurally non-decisional, the mechanism forecloses any distributed or consensus-based capital allocation and concentrates rural health AI deployment decisions in a single executive appointment.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Any organization competing for RHTP subrecipient funding — including AI vendors, tribal health organizations, and health system integrators — should submit complete applications before June 22 and prioritize direct engagement with the DOH Commissioner's office before mid-July, as no appeal mechanism, advisory body, or administrative intermediary can substitute for or override the Commissioner's selection decision.
